segments.t: KTPH000Plugins → AI Agent DesignKTPH001 decides how the runs of the terminal KTPH002AI agentKTPH003 are shown: as lines in the terminal itself, in a slim bar below or above it, on a rail or in a column beside it, as a card floating over it, in the classic activity panel, or in a combination of these. A KTPH004combinationKTPH005 picks one design for each role, and you can set one combination as the default and give single connections a different one.

Open it from KTPH000Plugins → AI Agent DesignKTPH001 or KTPH002View → AI Agent Panel → Design...KTPH003. With KTPH004open tool windows as tabsKTPH005 turned on it opens as a tab of the main window. An organisation policy that does not allow plugins locks both entries.
The table lists every design with its number, grouped by role. A tick in KTPH000ActiveKTPH001 chooses the design for its role in the shown combination, so each role always has exactly one tick.
Where the steps of a run are listed

KTPH000Blocks in the terminalKTPH001 (03), KTPH002Side timelineKTPH003 (02), KTPH004Plan and executionKTPH005 (06), KTPH006Card stackKTPH007 (07), KTPH008tmux paneKTPH009 (09), KTPH010ConversationKTPH011 (13), KTPH012Log tableKTPH013 (16), KTPH014Focus modeKTPH015 (17), KTPH016Classic panelKTPH017
A compact display of where the run stands, next to the history

KTPH000Metro lineKTPH001 (08), KTPH002Powerline status lineKTPH003 (01), KTPH004Minimap railKTPH005 (11), KTPH006Top bar with drawerKTPH007 (12), KTPH008Neon tickerKTPH009 (18), KTPH010Frosted glass HUDKTPH011 (04), KTPH012Spotlight and pillKTPH013 (05), KTPH014ToastsKTPH015 (10), KTPH016OrbitKTPH017 (15), KTPH018No status displayKTPH019
KTPH000In the historyKTPH001, KTPH002Suggestion at the cursor lineKTPH003 (14)
KTPH000FixedKTPH001, KTPH002Picture in pictureKTPH003 (19), KTPH004Adaptive dockKTPH005 (20)
A combination stored by a newer korTTY that names a design this version does not know uses the standard combination's design for that role instead.

KTPH000StandardKTPH001 is the default for every connection that does not pick its own combination; the default is marked with ★ in the list. The two built-in combinations cannot be changed: ticking another design while one of them is shown creates your own copy with that change. KTPH002NewKTPH003 starts a copy of the standard combination, KTPH004DuplicateKTPH005 copies the shown one, KTPH006RenameKTPH007 and KTPH008DeleteKTPH009 work on your own combinations, and KTPH010Use as DefaultKTPH011 makes the shown combination the default. Deleting the default makes KTPH012StandardKTPH013 the default again. Every change is saved at once.

The preview is a real terminal pane with a short shell session in which a sample run plays: the agent inspects the session, analyses, runs two commands, asks to shrink the journal, gets the answer KTPH0001KTPH001 and finishes with its answer. It uses your default terminal colours and font, a little smaller. Selecting a row in the table shows that design in the current combination without saving it; KTPH002ReplayKTPH003 starts the run again.

The run appears as a block directly above the shell's prompt line. Its header names the agent and your question, and shows the elapsed time and the reported tokens; below it there is one row per step with its result, and the running step turns a small spinner. korTTY writes the block into the terminal itself and sends nothing to the server, and the prompt line where you type is never rewritten, so you can keep typing the next command while the agent works.
KTPH005KTPH000KTPH006+KTPH007KTPH001KTPH008 shows or hides the details of the steps, KTPH009KTPH002KTPH010 or KTPH011KTPH003KTPH012+KTPH013KTPH004KTPH014 cancels the run.

An approval lists the planned commands with the keys KTPH0001KTPH001 (allow once), KTPH0022KTPH003 (allow always) and KTPH0043KTPH005 (cancel); while it is open these digits answer it and do not reach the shell.

When the run ends, the block collapses to a header with ✓ (or KTPH000cancelledKTPH001, KTPH002failedKTPH003), the number of steps, the time and the tokens, followed by the answer. The block then stays in the scrollback like any other output and goes into the session journal's capture.
The answer is part of the block, so the run dialog's KTPH000Show final answer in the terminal tooKTPH001 option only applies to combinations without blocks.

While a full-screen program such as KTPH000 or KTPH001 is open the block waits and catches up afterwards. A block that scrolled out of the screen during the run continues in a new block above the prompt.

A slim bar below the terminal draws the run as a metro line: one station per command, analysis and question, and an KTPH000AnswerKTPH001 station at the end. Reached stations are filled, the current one pulses, a station waiting for your input glows amber, and a light travels along the line as the run moves on; when there are more stations than fit, the oldest are summed up as KTPH002+NKTPH003. The bar also shows the question, the tokens and the time, and has buttons to pause, cancel and hide it.
The bar fades out a few seconds after the last run ended; the delay is set in the dialog. KTPH000View → AI Agent Panel → Show or Hide Status BarKTPH001 brings it back or hides it.

Like the KTPH000Metro lineKTPH001 (08), every display here follows the terminal's run that waits for input, or else its newest run still in progress, and fades out after the last run ended. KTPH002View → AI Agent Panel → Show or Hide Status BarKTPH003 brings any of them back or hides it. A display above or beside the terminal takes its room from the terminal while it is shown.

KTPH000Powerline status line (01)KTPH001 — One line below the terminal in powerline style: the agent, the step it works on with a spinner, how many commands it ran, the tokens and the time. ▴ unfolds the run's steps over the lowest terminal lines and ▾ folds them again; an open approval unfolds them by itself.

KTPH000Top bar with drawer (12)KTPH001 — A bar above the terminal, out of the way of the prompt and the newest output. A shimmering line shows that the agent works and turns green or red when the run ends; below it, the number of commands and the current step. ▾ drops the steps down over the older output.

KTPH001Minimap rail (11)KTPH002 — A narrow rail at the right edge of the terminal with one coloured segment per step: blue for commands, violet for analysis, amber for questions, red for errors. The running step glows. Pointing at a segment shows a lens with the step, its result and the first lines of its detail. The rail has no buttons; KTPH003KTPH000KTPH004 cancels the run.

KTPH000Neon ticker (18)KTPH001 — A bar in the style of a split-flap display below the terminal in the neon look of korTTY's logo: every new step rolls into its window, an open question glows amber with its keys, and the light at the left pulses while the agent works. On a light theme the bar uses the colours of that theme.

Instead of lines in the terminal, these designs list the run in a panel below or beside the terminal. A panel stays after the run ended, so its result can still be read; ✕ hides it until the next run, and KTPH000View → AI Agent Panel → Show or Hide Status BarKTPH001 brings it back. Every panel shows an open approval with its buttons, and the keys KTPH0021KTPH003, KTPH0042KTPH005 and KTPH0063KTPH007 answer it in the terminal as well. The answer is also written into the terminal as before.

KTPH000Side timeline (02)KTPH001 — A column right of the terminal with a vertical line and one node per step: commands in blue, analysis in violet, an open approval in amber with its buttons right at the node, the answer at the end. The line draws itself to each new node and the running node pulses. The terminal keeps its full height.

KTPH000Plan and execution (06)KTPH001 — Two columns below the terminal. On the left the run's steps as a checklist whose ticks draw themselves; on the right only what runs now: the command with its exit code and its last output lines, an open approval, or after the run the answer. A thin bar on top fills with the progress.

KTPH000Card stack (07)KTPH001 — Below the terminal, a narrow column with the question, the progress and the buttons, and beside it a stack of cards: the current step in front in full, the two before it peeking out behind. The mouse wheel leafs through the older steps; an approval is the front card with its buttons.

KTPH004tmux pane (09)KTPH005 — A pane right of the terminal in the terminal's font and colours, framed by lines: one line per step with its kind (KTPH000, KTPH001, KTPH002, KTPH003), the answer typed out behind a block cursor, and a blue status line at the bottom. It takes about 40 % of the width.

KTPH000Conversation (13)KTPH001 — A chat in a column right of the terminal: your question on the right, the agent on the left with its thoughts as text and its commands as code blocks with their exit code, which unfold to their output with a click. Three dots bounce while it works. The field below asks a follow-up question, which starts a new run in the same terminal once the current one ended.

KTPH000Log table (16)KTPH001 — A dense table below the terminal with the time, kind, step, result, duration and tokens of every step. A new row flashes blue, the running row has a small spinner, and an open approval puts its buttons into the header. A double-click on a row shows its output, on the last row the answer.
In the terminal: focus mode and the cursor lineKTPH000

KTPH001Focus mode (17)KTPH002 — A history design that writes what the agent does into the terminal as if it had typed it: each command as KTPH000 with its last output lines, its conclusions, an open approval with its keys, and after the run the answer. A glowing bar marks these lines, a light runs along under them while the agent works, and the rest of the terminal dims; the line you type in stays bright. When the run ends the terminal brightens again and the lines stay in the scrollback.

KTPH003Suggestion at the cursor line (14)KTPH004 — An approval design: the command the agent wants to run appears as ghost text right where you type, with a hint below it, and a line at the bottom of the terminal says that the agent waits. KTPH005KTPH000KTPH006 runs it once; KTPH007KTPH001KTPH008 takes it over: the run ends and the command is typed at the prompt for you to edit; KTPH009KTPH002KTPH010 declines. The keys KTPH0111KTPH012, KTPH0132KTPH014 and KTPH0153KTPH016 still answer as everywhere. A password request still uses the row below the terminal.
These status designs float over the terminal, which keeps its full size. They stay clear of the rows below the terminal and fade out after the last run ended, like the bars.

KTPH000Frosted glass HUD (04)KTPH001 — A translucent card over the bottom-right corner with the question, the step being run, the progress in segments and the tokens. While you type in the terminal it fades to 35 %, so the text under it stays readable. ⤢ unfolds the run's steps above it.

KTPH004Spotlight and pill (05)KTPH005 — A small pill in the top-right corner with the current step, how far the run got and the time; a click unfolds the steps below it. KTPH006View → AI Agent Panel → Ask in Spotlight…KTPH007 opens a field in the middle of the terminal where you ask the agent, with the profile to use and your earlier questions on KTPH008KTPH001KTPH009 and KTPH010KTPH002KTPH011. KTPH012KTPH003KTPH013 starts the run as KTPH000 at the shell would, and the field shrinks into the pill.

KTPH000Toasts (10)KTPH001 — Every finished step slides in as a short notice at the bottom right and goes again after a few seconds, a bar in each showing when. An approval stays until it is answered, with its buttons. A badge counts the steps; a click on it shows them all.

KTPH000Orbit (15)KTPH001 — A 72-pixel circle in the bottom-right corner: its ring fills with the run's progress, dots circle it while the agent works, and the middle shows the step count and the time; a label beside it names the current command. A click lets the steps bloom out of the circle.

KTPH000Picture in picture (19)KTPH001 — A small window floating over the terminal. Drag it by its title and it shows the four corners it can go to, then springs into the nearest one when you let go. ⧉ makes it a window of its own, for example for a second screen, and docks it back; – folds it to its title, × hides it until the next run. With a history panel in the combination the window holds that panel; otherwise it lists the run's steps and an open approval with its buttons. Several runs in the same terminal become tabs.

KTPH000Adaptive dock (20)KTPH001 — Picks the status display by the terminal's size: a wide and tall terminal (from 150 columns and 30 rows) gets the side timeline, a small one (under 70 columns or 16 rows) the status pill, anything between the Powerline status line. A display it chose stays until the size is clearly past the other side, so dragging a split does not make it flicker. After the last run a countdown ring shows how long the result stays.

An approval is answered with the keys KTPH0021KTPH003 (allow once), KTPH0042KTPH005 (allow always) and KTPH0063KTPH007 (cancel) in the terminal, or with buttons. Designs with buttons of their own show them: the history panels, the toasts and the picture-in-picture window. With blocks in the terminal, focus mode or the classic panel's history, an approval opens a row below the terminal with the commands and the buttons KTPH0081 Allow OnceKTPH009, KTPH0102 Allow AlwaysKTPH011 and KTPH0123 CancelKTPH013. A password request always opens that row, with a masked field, KTPH014Use for this SSH sessionKTPH015 and KTPH016OKKTPH017; KTPH018KTPH000KTPH019 submits and KTPH020KTPH001KTPH021 cancels. The classic panel keeps its own prompts.

Every design offers what the classic panel's buttons do. The bars, the history panels, the frosted glass HUD and the picture-in-picture window have a ⋯ button; the status pill, the orbit, the minimap rail and the badge of the toasts open the same menu with a right-click. It works on the run the design shows:
Turns the finished run into a reusable script, see KTPH000Generate Workflow ScriptKTPH001
Saves the finished run as Markdown, text, YAML, XML, JSON, PDF or Asciidoctor
Saves every finished run the terminal keeps in one file
Starts the same agent command again
Shows another run of the terminal: the ones still working and the last five that finished
The designs drawn into the terminal (blocks, focus mode, the suggestion at the cursor line) offer the same entries in the terminal's context menu under KTPH000AI → Last agent runKTPH001.

A right-click on a step opens its own menu with KTPH000Copy commandKTPH001, KTPH002Copy outputKTPH003, KTPH004Copy entryKTPH005 and KTPH006Open in Snippet EditorKTPH007. That works on a node of the side timeline, a row of the plan or the log table, a card of the stack, a block of the conversation, a line of the tmux pane, a segment of the minimap rail, a toast and a step in the picture-in-picture window.
Hide the status bar after a run after (seconds, 0 = keep)
How long the status display stays after the last run ended; 0 keeps it until you hide it. Default: 6 seconds.

Turns off the moving parts of every design: the pulsing station and the moving light of the KTPH000Metro lineKTPH001, the spinners, the shimmer of the KTPH002Top bar with drawerKTPH003, the rolling and glowing of the KTPH004Neon tickerKTPH005, the lens animation of the KTPH006Minimap railKTPH007, the sliding, popping and blooming of the history panels and floating displays, the typing of the KTPH008tmux paneKTPH009 and the ghost text, the glass of the KTPH010Frosted glass HUDKTPH011 and the fading of KTPH012Focus modeKTPH013.

The KTPH000AIKTPH001 tab of the KTPH002connection editorKTPH003 has an KTPH004AI agent designKTPH005 list: KTPH006Use the defaultKTPH007 (with the current default's name) or any combination. The choice applies from the next run on that connection. Because your own combinations live in this computer's settings, the choice is not part of an exported connection; a connection whose combination was deleted shows KTPH008Stored combination (currently unavailable)KTPH009 and uses the default.
